made_by: s2/s2loop/reason_video.py: the head-camera film with the trial's reason loop, colour-coded by phase

turns.say: first look at the table (agent look)
measure the paint tin's top and lid heights from depth before planning; nothing moves
fit the lid's plane and the rim height by direction, ask reach and the mask service for the lid; nothing moves
measure the press point on the lid's high side, its pixel, and whether parking poses beside the tin are in reach; nothing moves

the lid is a flat disc tilted 4.3 degrees (high side far-right, 5 to 7 mm proud of the rim); I will press its high side down once with the index fingertip, park the open hand beside the tin, measure the lid's plane, and press deeper once only if it is still tilted
press the lid's high side (28 mm uphill of its centre) straight down 10 mm with the index fingertip, slowly, once, per plan step 1
the press changed nothing on the lid (depth change 0.06 mm), so I locate the index fingertip at its hover from the robot's own depth layer to see whether it was over the press point; nothing moves
find where the index fingertip really stands at the hover, from the robot depth layer and the camera calibration, against where the press point is; nothing moves
map the hand's own depth around the hover to see how far along the pointing finger the camera sees and whether the fingertip can have reached the lid; nothing moves

the slow 10 mm press left the lid exactly as it was, so I re-execute the press as a real tap: faster (0.25 m/s), deeper (25 mm), 20 mm uphill of the centre, and stay pressed so the camera and the joints show what the lid does under the finger

under a 25 mm commanded press the hand stopped at the lid's surface (arm 39 mrad behind, finger bent) and the lid stayed tilted, so I measure from the first clean view where the lid's edge lies against the rim to learn how it is held; nothing moves

two fingertip presses left the lid exactly as it was and the second showed the hand stopped at the lid with the finger bending, so I change the skill to a knuckle tap with the closed fist written as my own program, after a clean look

turns.skill: plan_motion + execute_plan (linear up 7 cm, free to park, hand open)
turns.say: lift the pressing finger 7 cm straight up and park the open hand beside the tin, so that the lid is seen whole after the release and the next plan starts from a clean view (replan step R1)

measure the closed fist against the lid with solve_ik as a ruler (fingers down, palm toward the robot): how low the knuckles hang under the palm and where they are along the palm's facing direction; nothing moves (replan step R2)

the fist's lowest link (middle finger) hangs 11.6 cm under the palm origin; now scan the fist sideways and downhill over the tin's edge with solve_ik to find where that link sits relative to the palm origin; nothing moves

the lid's edge lies 45 mm from the tin's axis on its high side and 41 mm on its low side, so it sits about 2 mm toward the high side as if that edge rested on the rim; dry-run (no execution) a sideways nudge of the high edge with the pointing fingertip to see whether the planner accepts it

the measured edge shows the lid sits about 2 mm toward its high side with that edge standing over the rim, and a downward load between its two resting edges cannot move it, so I first nudge the high edge sideways toward the low side with the fingertip and keep the knuckle tap for after

turns.skill: plan_motion + execute_plan (pointing hand: hover, down, 8 mm sideways, up)
turns.say: set the pointing fingertip down just outside the lid's high edge, 1.5 mm over the far rim, and move it 8 mm toward the low side to nudge that edge off what it rests on, then rise (replan step N1)

the 8 mm nudge left the lid exactly as it was and the arm met no resistance (joint error 5 mrad), so the soft finger passed on under a newton; dry-run (no execution) a longer 26 mm pull with the finger held vertical so its tip stays hooked behind the lid's edge

dry-run (no execution) the knuckle tap from where the hand stands: fist with fingers down over the lid's high side, 3.5 cm hover, fast straight descent to 5 cm past first touch with an arm-torque guard, short stay, rise
turns.error: dry run refused: ik_unreachable at 78 % of the descent (joint 1 at its limit); nothing executed

turns.skill: plan_motion + execute_plan (vertical pointing finger: hover, down, 16 mm sideways, stop engaged)
turns.say: re-execute the nudge with changed parameters: finger held vertical so its tip stays hooked behind the lid's high edge, pull 16 mm toward the low side, and stop there with the finger still engaged so its joints show whether it holds the edge and what the lid does

the fingertip now holds the lid's high edge with about 1 N (finger joints bent back 0.08 rad) and neither lid nor tin moved, so I pull 7 mm further toward the low side and read the finger, the lid and the rim again

with the finger engaged the lid held against 1.15 N sideways and the fingertip then slipped over its edge, and the knuckle tap is refused beyond 3 cm (arm joint at its limit), so the last try inside the hand's envelope is a real tap: fingertip arriving at 0.40 m/s, twice, nearer the high edge

turns.skill: plan_motion + execute_plan (linear up 5 cm), guarded_press (2 presses)
turns.say: lift the finger 5 cm off the lid's edge, then tap the lid twice with the fingertip arriving at 0.40 m/s, 32 mm uphill of its centre (replan step T1)

the two fast taps met the lid (palm 22 mm behind its plan) and changed nothing, so I park the open hand beside the tin and measure the lid and the rim from a clear view for the ending (replan step T2)
the lid is as it was at the start and no ticks are left for another try; before closing I ask, without moving, whether the hammer on the table has a feasible grasp, as information for a later attempt
turns.error: propose_grasps: no_grasp (the words 'the hammer' returned the whole 39x29 cm tool cluster, which resembles no class with a clip)

turns.say: last look (agent look): lid as at the start, tin in place, hand open and 27 cm away; then close
